The new provider-backed deploy path can expose resolved secrets in persisted deploy metadata/logging, and provider verify/preflight commands are executed from `process.cwd()` instead of the target repo root, which breaks config-driven adapter commands that rely on repo-local scripts or relative paths.
`src/autonomy-v2/control-plane/service-auth.ts:185-189`, `src/autonomy-v2/commands/shared-github.ts:247-278, 332-342`, and `src/autonomy-v2/commands/deploy.ts:57-60` leak provider secrets through the recorded/displayed deploy command. `createProviderDeployExecution()` materializes templates with raw secret values, `normalizeDeployCommandConfig()` turns those args into `displayCommand`, and the deploy result/CLI output persists `deployCommand.command` without redaction. A provider that passes `{{apiToken}}` or similar via command/args will expose the secret in job results and status, violating the requirement that raw credentials never appear in status or chat-visible surfaces. Redaction currently only covers `deployCommand.output`, not the command string itself.
`src/autonomy-v2/control-plane/service-auth.ts:303-321, 371-405` runs provider verify/preflight/post-deploy commands relative to `process.cwd()` instead of the selected repo root. Because `executeProviderCommand()` calls `normalizeCommandConfig(..., process.cwd())`, any string/array command or relative `cwd` resolves against the bridge/server launch directory, not the repository being validated or deployed. That breaks the config-driven adapter contract for providers implemented with repo-local scripts or relative paths, and there is no focused test covering repo-relative provider commands.

`src/autonomy-v2/control-plane/service-auth.ts:487-490` now prefers `process.env` for secret resolution, but bridge status processing loads repo env files into the shared process with `loadAutonomyEnv(repoRoot)` (`src/env/env-main.ts:11-19,35-47`; `src/server/control-plane/control-plane-bridge.ts:586-590`).
